why: A social-evaluative stressor such as public speaking or an exam reliably raises subjective anxiety and tension.
Acute stress activates the sympathetic system and HPA axis (heart rate, adrenaline, cortisol), so people feel keyed-up and alert.
Negative affect rises and positive affect falls during a stressor, recovering within roughly an hour afterwards.
Stress hormones and catecholamines impair prefrontal working memory and flexible attention, though simple well-learned tasks can be spared or helped.

Stress-induced analgesia via endogenous opioids and descending inhibition is robust in animals but small and inconsistent with psychological stressors in humans (some studies show stress-induced hyperalgesia).

why: People with generalised anxiety report higher subjective anxiety and worry during and after a stressor, even when hormonal responses are similar or blunted.

compare: typical profile in the same situation
why: In depression, negative mood after a stressor is larger and recovers more slowly (rumination), although cortisol reactivity itself is often blunted rather than increased.
source: Burke 2005 meta-analysis; Bylsma 2008 emotional reactivity meta-analysis

why: Autistic adults report higher subjective anxiety under social-evaluative stress, while physiological cortisol responses are mixed (often similar or blunted).
A single 20-60 min bout of moderate aerobic exercise reliably increases positive activated affect for an hour or more.
State anxiety falls modestly after an acute bout of aerobic exercise, similar in size to quiet rest or meditation.
Exercise-induced hypoalgesia raises pain thresholds for minutes to about half an hour, involving endogenous opioid and endocannabinoid release; effects are variable and weaker in chronic pain.
Moderate-to-vigorous exercise briefly suppresses appetite ('exercise-induced anorexia', lower ghrelin), without much compensatory eating the same day.
Daytime exercise has small positive effects on sleep onset and quality that evening; felt sleepiness at bedtime may be slightly higher but the effect is modest.
Vigorous exercise ending within about an hour of bedtime keeps arousal high and delays sleep onset, whereas moderate evening exercise earlier does not harm sleep.
Regular exercise over weeks reduces depressive symptoms with moderate effect sizes, comparable to psychotherapy or antidepressants in some trials.
source: Schuch 2016 meta-analysis; Noetel 2024 BMJ network meta-analysis

why: Bright light acutely increases subjective alertness via intrinsically photosensitive retinal cells, though daytime effects are smaller and less consistent than at night.
Bright light in the late evening suppresses melatonin, delays the circadian clock and makes people feel less sleepy.
Plenty of daytime bright light advances circadian timing and reduces sensitivity to evening light, so people tend to feel sleepy somewhat earlier in the evening.
Daily morning bright light therapy over weeks improves mood in seasonal and, less strongly, non-seasonal depression.
Friendly face-to-face contact directly increases felt closeness and connection.
Experience-sampling studies consistently show higher positive affect during and after pleasant social interaction, even with weak ties.
source: Sandstrom & Dunn 2014; Kahneman 2004 Day Reconstruction Method

why: Support from a close friend or partner before a stressor buffers subjective anxiety and cortisol responses (social buffering).
Holding a partner's hand or having supportive company slightly reduces reported pain, but effects vary with relationship quality and support style.
A satisfying meal produces satiety through stomach stretch, gut hormones (CCK, GLP-1, PYY) and falling ghrelin, lasting a few hours.
The sight, smell and anticipation of tasty food trigger dopamine-driven 'wanting'; this falls again once people are full (sensory-specific satiety).
Eating tasty food gives a brief rise in pleasure and positive mood that typically fades within an hour or two.
Background noise and visual clutter compete for attention and modestly impair demanding cognitive tasks.
For most typical adults an ordinary shopping centre is mildly stimulating but does not meaningfully raise anxiety.
source: expert judgement; Ellermeier & Hellbrück noise annoyance literature

why: Acute pain activates the sympathetic nervous system and grabs attention, raising heart rate and alertness.
Pain is by definition an unpleasant experience and lowers mood while it lasts.
Pain raises worry and threat feelings, more so when it is unexplained or uncontrollable.
After one night of about 4-5 hours, subjective sleepiness the next morning is clearly increased.
Sustained attention (lapses on vigilance tasks) is most affected by sleep loss; one short night gives a noticeable but not dramatic drop.
Sleep loss reduces positive affect and increases irritability, with the largest effect on positive mood.
Sleep loss increases anxiety symptoms and amygdala reactivity, especially in people already prone to anxiety.
Short sleep raises ghrelin, lowers leptin and increases appetite for energy-dense food, adding roughly 250-400 kcal intake the next day.
Paradoxically, sleep deprivation (best shown for total or late-night deprivation) lifts mood transiently in about half of depressed patients, usually relapsing after recovery sleep.
source: Boland 2017 meta-analysis; Wirz-Justice & Van den Hoofdakker 1999
